card.title: Atomic Mass, Isotopes and Mass Defect

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **atomic mass unit** is 1/12 of carbon-12: 1 u = 1.66×10⁻²⁷ kg. **Isotopes** share Z but differ in A (¹H, ²H, ³H; ³⁵Cl/³⁷Cl), **isobars** share A (⁴⁰Ar/⁴⁰Ca), **isotones** share N; chlorine's 35.5 u is the weighted average (75% × 35 + 25% × 37). Radioactive isotopes decay with **decay constant** λ — the per-second decay probability (NEB 2024, 2m): N = N₀e^(−λt), half-life T₁/₂ = 0.693/λ, mean life τ = 1/λ.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - N = N₀e^(−λt) - T₁/₂ = 0.693/λ; τ = 1/λ - Fraction after n half-lives: (1/2)ⁿ - 1 u = 1.66×10⁻²⁷ kg

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Mass Defect Definition:** $\Delta m = Z m_p + N m_n - M_{\text{nucleus}}$ where $m_p \approx 1.007276$ u, $m_n \approx 1.008665$ u. The defect is always positive — the bound nucleus is lighter than its free constituents.  ·  **Binding Energy Conversion:** $BE = \Delta m \cdot c^2 = \Delta m \times 931.494$ MeV. The binding energy is the energy needed to separate the nucleus into free nucleons. It is positive for bound nuclei.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The decay constant is the probability per unit time that a nucleus will decay."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2023*** — 8-day half-life: after 24 days, 1/8 remains; 800 Bq → 100 Bq.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Same Element, Different Weight Chlorine's atomic "mass" is 35.5 — yet no chlorine atom weighs that. Nature makes the same element in several masses (**isotopes**), and the periodic table lists their weighted average. Half-life governs how fast radioactive isotopes vanish.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2023, 2024, 2020) ### 2.1 Atomic mass unit and atomic mass - **Atomic mass unit:** 1 u = 1/12 the mass of a neutral $_{6}^{12}C$ atom = **1.66×10⁻²⁷ kg**. - Proton ≈ 1.0073 u, neutron ≈ 1.0087 u, electron ≈ 0.00055 u. - An element's **atomic mass** on the periodic table is the weighted average of its naturally occurring isotopes.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "n = t/T₁/₂; fraction = (1/2)ⁿ; multiply the initial activity by the same fraction."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (2m): A sample of half-life 10 days decays for 30 days. What fraction remains?** — n = 3 → (1/2)³ = 1/8.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Define λ, quote T₁/₂ = ln2/λ and τ = 1/λ — three relations in one line.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Isotope Chemistry vs Nuclear Properties:** Isotopes (same Z, different A) have identical chemical properties (electron configuration) but different nuclear masses, stabilities, and half-lives. Chemical separation is impossible; nuclear methods (centrifugation, diffusion, laser) are required.  ·  **Isotopes: same Z. Isobars: same A. Isotones: same N** — three families, three different fixed numbers.  ·  **T₁/₂ = 0.693/λ, not 1/λ** — the ln 2 matters.
